entities.description: A network or security zone. `access` means an attacker can originate traffic there, not that every member is compromised.
entities.meaning: A network or zone. Being in it means the attacker can send traffic there.

entities.description: A forwarding and management device. `admin` means administrative control.
entities.meaning: Forwards traffic between networks and can be administered.

entities.description: The filter managed by one router. Its permissions apply to named flows.
entities.meaning: A router's filter: which flows it lets through.

entities.description: A workstation or server. `user` and `admin` control are distinct.
entities.meaning: A machine: a workstation, a server, a virtual machine or a container. It may run on another host.

entities.description: Client-side software running on a host or router.
entities.meaning: Software that makes connections, e.g. a browser or mail client. Reached only through what it opens.

entities.description: A reachable service running on a host or router, with exploit and login routes.
entities.meaning: Software that accepts connections, e.g. a web server or SSH. Exploited or logged into over the network.

entities.description: One software version, e.g. OpenSSH 9.6. Its services share one exploit discovery; patching is set here.
entities.meaning: A software version. Every service that is an instance of it shares its vulnerabilities.

entities.description: An identity with explicit authentication and grants; no implicit global privileges. Multi-factor login is its switch.
entities.meaning: An identity that services accept and that has rights on machines.

entities.description: A description of authentication material; `possessed` is the attacker holding it. Never the secret itself.
entities.meaning: What proves an account, e.g. a password or key. Must be extracted from where it is kept.

entities.description: A human user who reads content and can be deceived. `knows` and `operates` say what deceit gives away.
entities.meaning: A person who reads mail or pages and can be deceived into acting.

associations.description: Membership of a network; a machine can be attached to several. Implies no flow permission.
The machine an executable, a router or a guest host runs on, at `privilege: user | admin`. Each has one host; a router or a guest runs only on a host.
The firewall a router manages: one each way.
Where a credential is kept: a host at `privilege: user | admin`, an application as `user`. Possession still takes an extraction.
A credential that proves an account: as its first factor (any one suffices) or, with `factor: second`, as the second.
A service that accepts this account for login.
What an account gets on a host (`user | admin`) or router (`admin` only).
Management access to a machine from a network, independent of ordinary forwarding.
A firewall's named permission for a flow: `allowed: true | false | unknown`.
The software version a service runs: exactly one product.
The identity a workload runs as: a host at `privilege: user | admin`, software as `user`. Code in it can use the identity without credentials.
An account that may become another, e.g. a role it can assume.
A credential a person could disclose when deceived.
Software a person uses; deceived, they run what they are sent in it.
Content from anyone in this network reaches the person: mail, a public web page.

states.description: Traffic can be originated in this network.
This software does what the attacker says.
Content the attacker controls is in front of this reader.
This person acts on what the attacker sent.

defenses.description: The vendor fix is applied: `find-exploit-patched` stands in for `find-exploit`.
Where the credential is kept is hardened: `extract-protected` stands in for `extract`.
The account needs a second factor: a first factor alone no longer logs in.
The person is trained against deception: `phish-trained` stands in for `phish`.

parameters.name: Connect
parameters.description: Time to establish the flow once its source is controlled and its route permitted.

parameters.name: Find an exploit
parameters.description: Time to find a usable exploit for a software version, once an instance is reachable.

parameters.name: Find an exploit (patched)
parameters.description: The same, once the product is patched; selected by `defenses.patched`.

parameters.name: Use the exploit
parameters.description: Time to turn a found exploit into control of the service.

parameters.name: Log in
parameters.description: Time to log in with an account's material, once the service is reachable.

parameters.name: Extract
parameters.description: Time to extract the credential from a store the attacker controls.

parameters.name: Extract (protected)
parameters.description: The same, once the store is protected; selected by `defenses.protected`.

parameters.name: Admin login
parameters.description: Time to authenticate to a machine's management from an administering network.

parameters.name: Escape to the host
parameters.description: Time to break out of a virtual machine, container or appliance to the host it runs on, once in admin control of it.

parameters.name: Get past multi-factor login
parameters.description: Time to get past the second factor once a first factor is held: push fatigue, a proxy, a SIM swap — the note says which.

parameters.name: Deceive
parameters.description: Time until the person acts on a lure once content reaches them.

parameters.name: Deceive (trained)
parameters.description: The same, once the person is trained; selected by `defenses.trained`.

rules.title: The attacker starts here
rules.prerequisites: a declared foothold
rules.output: the named state, attained at time zero
assumptions: A foothold is an attacker input, never an estimate of an initial compromise.

rules.title: Admin control includes user control
rules.prerequisites: host.admin
assumptions: Administrative control of a host includes everything a user can do on it.

rules.title: Controlling a machine controls its software
rules.prerequisites: the hosting machine at the executable's declared privilege (admin also satisfies user)
rules.scope: one per hosts association naming an executable
assumptions: Controlling a machine at the privilege software runs with is controlling that software.
Router-hosted executables run as admin: this library has no router user state.

rules.title: Controlled software acts with its privilege
rules.prerequisites: executable.control
rules.output: the hosting machine at the executable's declared privilege
rules.scope: one per hosts association naming an application or service
assumptions: Controlling software yields the privilege it runs with and no more: user software never alone grants admin.

rules.title: Controlling the host controls its router
rules.prerequisites: the hosting host at the router's declared privilege (admin also satisfies user)
rules.scope: one per hosts association naming a router
assumptions: Whoever controls the machine a router runs on, at the privilege it runs with, controls the router.
Leaving the router for its host is its own timed step, the router's escape.

rules.title: Controlling the host controls its guests
rules.prerequisites: the hosting host at the guest's declared privilege (admin also satisfies user)
rules.scope: one per hosts association naming a host
assumptions: Whoever controls a hypervisor or container host at the privilege a guest runs with controls the guest.

rules.title: Escape to the host
rules.prerequisites: guest host.admin
rules.output: the hosting host at the guest's declared privilege
assumptions: Breaking out of a virtual machine or container is one timed step; hardening it is an edit of that time.

rules.title: Escape from the router to its host
rules.prerequisites: router.admin, for a router that runs on a host
rules.output: the hosting host at the router's declared privilege
assumptions: Leaving a router VM or appliance for its host is one timed step.

rules.title: A controlled machine reaches its networks
rules.prerequisites: host.user or router.admin, for a machine attached to the network
assumptions: Access to a network is the capability to originate traffic in it, not control of its members.

rules.title: The firewall lets the flow through
rules.prerequisites: the permission's policy allows the flow, or the managing router is under admin control
rules.output: the flow's permission at that firewall, satisfied
assumptions: A router's admin can bypass its firewall for an explicitly modelled flow.
An unknown policy is an unknown branch, not a denial.

rules.title: Connect along the flow
rules.prerequisites: source.control and every permission along the route
assumptions: The route is checked statically; there is no discovery of IP routes, NAT or transitive trust.

rules.title: A connection reaches the service
rules.prerequisites: any inbound flow.connected
assumptions: Reaching a service is not controlling it.

rules.title: An instance is reachable
rules.prerequisites: service.reachable, for any instance of the product
assumptions: Any one reachable instance is enough to study the software version.

rules.title: Find an exploit
rules.prerequisites: product.reachable
assumptions: Patching selects the authored replacement distribution; it does not by itself eliminate every exploit.
An exploit found through one instance works on every instance of the same version; a partly patched fleet is two products.

rules.title: Use the exploit
rules.prerequisites: product.exploit-ready and the service's own reachable
assumptions: Deployment includes whatever bypass of detection or protection the author assumed in its note; there is no unreported extra success factor.

rules.title: Extract a credential
rules.prerequisites: the storing host at the store's privilege, or the storing application under control
assumptions: Protection selects the authored replacement distribution, not a guarantee.
Possession requires an extraction action even from a controlled store.

rules.title: A held credential unlocks its account
rules.prerequisites: credential.possessed, for a credential that authenticates the account as its first factor
assumptions: Any one first-factor credential gives the material; a second factor alone gives none.
Material alone grants no access.

rules.title: Multi-factor login is off
rules.prerequisites: the account's `mfa` switch is off
assumptions: An unknown switch is an unknown branch, not a guess either way.

rules.title: A second factor is held
rules.prerequisites: credential.possessed, for a credential that authenticates the account with `factor: second`
assumptions: A hardware key, an authenticator seed or a stolen session cookie in the attacker's hands is the second factor.

rules.title: Get past multi-factor login
rules.prerequisites: account.material
assumptions: Push fatigue, adversary-in-the-middle proxies and SIM swaps are one timed step; the note says which the value stands for.

rules.title: The account can log in
rules.prerequisites: account.material and account.mfa-satisfied
assumptions: With multi-factor login off, a first factor alone authenticates.

rules.title: Running code uses its identity
rules.prerequisites: the workload under control, or its host at the declared privilege
assumptions: Whoever runs code in the workload can obtain its identity's token; metadata-endpoint hardening stops remote request forgery, not code execution, so it is not a switch here.
The token is still used through an ordinary login to a service that authorizes the account.

rules.title: Become another role
rules.prerequisites: the first account authenticated
assumptions: Trust-policy conditions (external id, required MFA, source address) are not modelled.

rules.title: Content from a zone reaches a reader
rules.prerequisites: network.access
assumptions: Anyone who can send traffic in the zone can put content in front of the reader: mail from the internet, a public ticket queue.

rules.title: A controlled service reaches its readers
rules.prerequisites: control of a service that a flow from an application the person operates targets
rules.scope: one per flow from an application a person operates
assumptions: Watering holes, poisoned retrieval stores and compromised tool servers are this rule.

rules.title: Deceive a person
rules.prerequisites: person.contacted
assumptions: Training selects the authored replacement distribution; it does not make a person undeceivable.

rules.title: A deceived person discloses what they know
rules.prerequisites: person.deceived
assumptions: What a person knows is what they could type into a convincing fake login.

rules.title: A deceived person runs what they are sent
rules.prerequisites: person.deceived
assumptions: Which consequences of deceit exist — disclosure, running something — is the author's choice of associations.

rules.title: Log in to a service
rules.prerequisites: service.reachable and account.authenticated, for an account the service authorizes
assumptions: Retries and account lockout are outside this library.

rules.title: A login gives the account's rights
rules.prerequisites: account.session at a service, and a grant on the machine that hosts that service
rules.output: the hosting machine at the granted privilege
rules.scope: one per matching session and grant
assumptions: A grant is used only on the machine the service actually runs on; a login on one machine is never control of another.

rules.title: Admin login from a network
rules.prerequisites: access to the administering network and account.authenticated, for an account granted on the managed machine
rules.output: the managed machine at the granted privilege
rules.scope: one per administration and grant pair
assumptions: An administration association is explicit permission to attempt management authentication, not a successful login.
An isolated administration zone is not reached just because it administers something.
